subject.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups

question: Should subscription-auth helper dispatch be a generic core embedded-run capability driven by provider-owned CLI backend metadata, or should core permanently own Claude-CLI-specific eligibility policy?
rationale: The observable bug is established, but repository policy places provider-specific auth and routing behavior with the provider owner while core should expose generic seams; choosing the permanent boundary affects future helper paths and the security-sensitive MCP grant contract.

options.title: Provider capability seam
options.body: Add provider-owned CLI backend capability metadata for subscription-auth helper dispatch and keep the core dispatcher generic, using the same eligibility result for timeout selection.

options.title: Approve core Claude policy
options.body: Keep the submitted Claude-CLI-specific core eligibility logic and explicitly accept core ownership of credential-sensitive provider routing.

options.title: Unify helper dispatch first
options.body: Pause this PR and implement the broader helper-runtime routing design tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57326 before landing an active-memory-specific opt-in.

recommendation.title: Provider capability seam
recommendation.body: Add provider-owned CLI backend capability metadata for subscription-auth helper dispatch and keep the core dispatcher generic, using the same eligibility result for timeout selection.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on canonical Anthropic-to-Claude-CLI runtime routing is the closest history signal for deciding where this provider-dispatch policy belongs.
